- AGENTS.md + Codex CLI + gpt-5.2-codex: time 129.91 s / 70.34 s; output tokens 4,591.46 / 2,440.00; input 318,651.51 / 120,587.00; cached input 296,078.73 / 104,448.00; total 619,321.70 / 226,582.00. Quality: not measured (sanity check only)

fields.v: Tasks: 124 merged PRs from 10 repos, rebuilt as issue-style task statements generated by gpt-oss-120b from the PR diff and file tree. Configurations: with vs without root AGENTS.md (file removed, all else unchanged). Baseline: without AGENTS.md. Held constant: agent (Codex CLI), model (gpt-5.2-codex), task input, repository snapshot, fresh Docker container per repo, reset between tasks. Acceptance tests: none (no correctness evaluation). Repetitions: Not stated (apparently one run per condition per task). Human intervention: none during runs

AGENTS.md better on efficiency: median wall-clock time -28.64% (98.57 -> 70.34 s), mean -20.27%; median output tokens -16.58% (2,925 -> 2,440), mean -20.08%. Input, cached input and total tokens: means -9.7 to -9.97%, medians -0.99 to -3.41% (slightly higher with AGENTS.md). Significant (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p<0.05) only for wall-clock time and output tokens. Task completion described as 'comparable' (not measured)

Distinguished conditions on time and output tokens, not on total tokens. Repeatability: code, Dockerfiles and generated tasks released; number of runs per condition not stated (apparently one), agent stochasticity acknowledged. Limitations stated: sampled subset of repositories, PRs and agent configurations; one agent framework and model; small-scope PRs; no correctness evaluation; effects may depend on agent stochasticity

rev.why: The value stated 'single run per condition' as fact; the paper does not give the number of runs (p. 3-4), as the Comparison: design field already notes
